question:
Given the following 3x3 system representing the intersection of three planes:

$x + 2y + 3z = 1$
$2x + 5y + 8z = 3$
$3x + 8y + 14z = 4$

(a) Use the matrix method to determine if the system has a unique solution.
(b) If so, find the solution vector $\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}$.

options.A:
(a) $|A|=0$, so the system does not have a unique solution.
(b) Therefore, a unique solution vector cannot be found.
options.B:
(a) $|A|=1\ne0$, so the system has a unique solution.
(b) $X=\begin{bmatrix}-2\\3\\-1\end{bmatrix}$.
options.C:
(a) $|A|=1\ne0$, so the system has a unique solution.
(b) $X=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-3\\1\end{bmatrix}$.
options.D:
(a) $|A|=-1\ne0$, so the system has no solution.
(b) No solution vector exists.
